Cosmetic dentistry is all about helping patients feel confident in their smiles. But with so many practices offering similar services, how do you stand out and get noticed?

The right [cosmetic dental marketing](https://delmain.co/dental-marketing/) strategies can help you reach patients who care about aesthetics and are ready to invest in their smiles. Let’s break down proven strategies — plus a couple of bonus ideas — to help your practice grow.

## 1\. Attract patients with a modern, high-performance website

Your [dental website](https://delmain.co/dental-website-design/) is your practice’s first impression. A polished, professional website helps patients feel confident in your skills before they even step through the door.

Here’s what sets a great cosmetic dental website apart:

*   Modern, mobile-friendly design: Make sure your site looks beautiful and functions perfectly on any device.
*   Original, high-quality photography: Skip the generic stock photos. Showcase your actual team, office, and results to build trust and highlight your work.
*   Fast load times: A slow site makes patients click away. Optimize images and site performance to keep visitors engaged.
*   Easy online booking: Patients expect convenience — make it simple for them to schedule a consultation.

And don’t forget SEO. A fast, visually appealing site that’s optimized with the right keywords helps your practice rank higher and attract more of the right patients.

## Get inspired by this year’s best dental website designs

[Read Now](https://delmain.co/blog/best-dental-websites/)

## 2\. Tailor your message to cosmetic dental patients

The foundation of any successful cosmetic dentistry marketing strategy is a deep understanding of your target audience. Addressing the specific needs and desires of these patients requires a tailored approach.

While zeroing in on your marketing messaging, keep the following in mind.

### Identify concerns and provide solutions

Understand the questions and hesitations potential patients have regarding cosmetic procedures, offering clear and reassuring answers.

Patients seeking cosmetic dental treatments often come with specific aesthetic issues that affect their confidence and overall well-being. These concerns can include teeth discoloration, misalignment, gaps, or chipped teeth. To tailor your message effectively, it’s crucial to empathize with these concerns and provide solutions that resonate with your target audience.

### Showcase real-life transformations

Authenticity builds trust, so use real patient stories and testimonials to illustrate how you’ve transformed smiles and lives.

Patients want to see concrete evidence of the results your practice can deliver. Including before-and-after photographs of actual patients who have undergone cosmetic treatments is a persuasive way to build trust and motivate potential patients.

### Maintain a consistent brand voice

Your brand voice encompasses the tone, style, and messaging used in all your marketing materials, from your website to social media content, and even printed materials.

A consistent brand voice enhances your practice’s credibility and makes it instantly recognizable to both current and potential patients. It also reinforces the trustworthiness of your cosmetic dental services, as patients will perceive your practice as reliable and professional.

## 3\. Optimize your presence with Search Engine Optimization (SEO)

Attracting new patients in today's competitive dental landscape takes more than just having a great smile—it requires standing out in a crowded market. Adopting innovative cosmetic dentistry marketing ideas can make all the difference for patient acquisition and long-term practice growth. In this post, we explore ten creative strategies to increase patient acquisition and grow your practice.

## **Essential Cosmetic Dental Marketing Strategies**

### Understand the Cosmetic Dentistry Market

Before diving into specific tactics, it's essential to gain an understanding of the cosmetic dentistry market and its trends and challenges. Patients today expect personalized experiences online - they seek information about treatments, patient testimonials and before-and-after galleries as they research options for themselves. With increasing competition comes increased emphasis on developing effective cosmetic dentistry marketing strategies - this means understanding target markets, patient demographics and industry trends before devising effective plans to promote your services.

### Optimize Your Online Presence

An effective online presence is at the core of modern marketing plans. Your website often acts as the first impression prospective patients get of your practice, so make sure it is professionally designed, mobile-friendly, and optimized for search engines using SEO best practices such as targeting keywords, optimizing images and producing valuable content - this will increase visibility while building trust among prospective patients searching for reliable cosmetic dentistry services. Additionally, check out our [dental SEO strategies](https://www.remedo.io/blog/seo-strategies-for-dentists) improve visibility while building trust among prospective patients searching for reliable cosmetic dentistry services.

### Leverage Social Media Marketing

Social media platforms like Instagram, Facebook and TikTok can be invaluable tools for engaging your target audience and showcasing your work. Visual platforms are especially beneficial when showcasing cosmetic dentistry techniques like before-and-after photos, patient testimonials and live Q&A sessions can demonstrate expertise. By posting engaging and educational content that builds community around your practice and enhances brand loyalty you can strengthen community bonds while simultaneously drawing in new patients. Social media also allows targeted advertising which can refine outreach efforts and generate more qualified leads. For more tips, explore our [social media post ideas for dentists](https://www.remedo.io/blog/dental-social-media-post-ideas).

### Embrace Content Marketing Innovation

Content is the king in today's digital landscape. High-quality, informative content helps educate potential patients about cosmetic procedures, the benefits of various treatments, and industry trends. Blog posts, videos, and infographics build credibility while simultaneously increasing search engine ranking. Develop a blog on your website to get more cosmetic dentistry leads. Use your content calendar to address common patient inquiries while also showcasing your expertise; an effective cosmetic dentistry marketing plan often revolves around providing valuable content that establishes you as a trusted source.

### Enhance Your Email Marketing Campaigns

[Email marketing for doctors](https://www.remedo.io/marketing-services/healthcare-email-marketing) and dentists remains one of the most effective strategies to build patient loyalty and retain leads. Create engaging newsletters featuring exclusive offers, updates on new treatments and educational information related to oral care. Segment your mailing lists so that messages tailored specifically for each patient arrive. By communicating regularly and offering valuable services through regular, valuable communication channels with patients you can increase appointment bookings while building long-term loyalty.

### Utilize Online Reviews and Reputation Management

Patient testimonials play an integral part in building trust between providers and patients. Encourage happy patients to leave reviews on platforms like Google, Yelp, or your own website to demonstrate that you value feedback and strive for continuous improvement. Active [reputation management](https://www.remedo.io/reputation-management) strengthens credibility while making your practice more appealing to newcomers looking into cosmetic dentistry options.

### Run Targeted PPC and Digital Advertising

Organic reach is important, but investing in targeted digital ads can accelerate patient acquisition. Platforms like Google Ads and Facebook Ads enable you to run targeted advertising campaigns targeting specific demographics, geographic areas and interests - ideal for running campaigns to highlight your unique value proposition and clear calls-to-action ad copy that stands out against competition.

_This week’s blog post comes from the “Ask Sabri” column in our magazine. As it addresses a question that is highly relevant to many dental practice owners right now, we wanted to share it on our blog, as well. Enjoy!_

## Q: What kind of marketing should we do to get more patients for cosmetic and full-mouth services?

Great question! For this, I would separate marketing into two categories: _marketing to your patients of record_ and _publicly advertising for new patients_.

Typically, offices that do a high volume of cosmetic dentistry have a large patient base from GP services and that’s where they generate the majority of their cosmetic cases.

And I say the word “generate” intentionally, because no matter how large your patient base is, cosmetic cases don’t just fall into your lap. Well…a few probably will, but you’ll also be missing out on a ton of cases if you aren’t active about finding them in your patient base.

So, the first priority is always to simply increase general patient volume (between hygiene, reactivation, and new patients), and market cosmetic services to these patients-of-record.

Then you can add strategic new patient marketing on top of that.

Certainly, there are people out there looking for veneers, Invisalign, smile makeovers, large restorative cases, etc., so you can and should advertise publicly. However, marketing cosmetic services directly to new patients can be a little tricky and expensive, so you need to be smart about it.

## Marketing to Your Patients-of-Record

### Don’t assume your patients already know which services you offer

I can’t even count the number of times I’ve spoken to a dentist that was flabbergasted to find out a long-term, loyal patient had gone elsewhere for clear aligners or veneers and then came back for their usual recall visit. When the dentist asks why they didn’t just do the clear aligners here, the patient says, “Oh, I had no idea you do clear aligners! I would have preferred to do them with you.”

So, it is always ironic to see a dentist aggressively advertising to the broader community (which is expensive) while doing very little to make their own patients aware of their servic­­es (which is very easy and affordable).

## Ways to find more cosmetic cases among your patient base

Here are the things I would recommend doing to market and close cosmetic cases to your patients-of-record. This isn’t an exhaustive list, but these are the essentials:

*   **Do a brief cosmetic questionnaire with _every_ patient while they are in the chair**—and repeat it at each annual exam because things can change over time. ([See this article from Dr. Michael Ofir](https://www.mgeonline.com/2017/4-tips-getting-cosmetic-dentistry-cases/) for more on this questionnaire.)
*   **Send text message (SMS) promotions to your patients**. There are plenty of text messaging services out there and you may already be using them for appointment![marketing channels](/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/2.jpg.webp) confirmations or reactivation. Consider using it to offer a free consultation for implants, Invisalign, smile makeover, etc.
*   **Have lots of promotional material around your office.** This includes posters, flyers, videos, before-and-after photos, etc. Put them up anywhere a patient’s eyes may be looking at any point; the waiting room, in front of or over the dental chair, front desk countertop, hallways, restrooms, etc.
*   **Send email promotions**. Email marketing is vastly underutilized in dentistry. You can send promotional offers about these services, as well as write informative content about them in a monthly e-newsletter. Always include an attractive offer like a free consult or discount.
*   **Post relevant content on social media**. Ideally, a large portion of your patient base should be following you on social media. (If you don’t know how to leverage social media effectively, attend the [MGE New Patient Workshop](https://www.newpatients.net/)!) So, post informative videos from the doctor, patient testimonials, smile reveal videos, before-and-after photos, etc. Again, include an attractive offer.
*   **Ensure your staff are educated on these services—so they can in turn educate** **patients**. Your staff can’t educate patients about cosmetic services if they don’t have understanding themselves. So do some “lunch & learns” with your team. You may even consider offering your team an incentive structure, where if the hygienist or assistant, for example, gets a patient interested in a service (and then patient pays for the service), they receive a commission. Although, you will want to keep an eye on this so that staff aren’t awkwardly shoehorning it into conversations with patients who aren’t interested.

## Advertising for New Patients

Things like Google ads, targeted social media ads, implant funnels, and direct mail can get pretty pricey. That’s okay _if_ the marketing is working and you are scheduling and closing new patients for high-ticket services.

### Three Keys to Marketing Cosmetic & Large Restorative Services Successfully

Each of these types of marketing _can_ be effective. I’ve seen them all work well—but _only_ if you do three things well:

1.  #### Put a BIG focus on how incoming leads are handled
    
    This is BY FAR the biggest problem I see with dental offices trying to advertise cosmetic services and big cases: not enough attention is put on how incoming phone calls are handled or how quickly appointment requests are followed up with.
